title: Explosion kills Ukrainian prisoners of war at the Olenivka detention facility
body:
On 29 July 2022 an explosion hit a barrack holding Ukrainian prisoners of war at a Russian-run prison in Molodizhne, near Olenivka in Donetsk Oblast. Most of the prisoners were soldiers of the Azov Regiment who had defended the Azovstal plant in Mariupol. Estimates of the toll range from 53 to more than 62 dead and from 75 to more than 130 wounded. Russia reported 53 dead and 75 wounded, while Ukraine reported about 40 dead and 130 wounded. Of the 53 confirmed dead, nine survived the initial blast but died without medical care.

Russia blamed a Ukrainian HIMARS rocket strike, and Ukraine said Russian forces were responsible. On 3 August 2022 UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres announced a fact-finding mission that both sides had requested, but Russia then refused to cooperate with the UN and the International Committee of the Red Cross, and on 3 January 2023 the UN disbanded the mission, saying it could not deploy to the site. In March 2023 the UN human rights office reported that guards were repositioned, a trench was dug and a Grad rocket system fired nearby, possibly masking the blasts. An October 2023 UN report said the damage was inconsistent with a HIMARS strike.

CNN, the Associated Press and others have published analyses pointing away from the Russian account, and Ukraine appealed to the International Criminal Court, according to the Wikipedia article.
